overall: The AG resolved the complaint by informal action and found no Open Meeting Law violation: Chair and Vice Chair meetings with the superintendent were not deliberations, and agenda-authority questions fall outside the law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Chair and Vice Chair regularly discussed matters with the superintendent outside meetings to decide which items go to the Committee.
allegations.key_passage: Where the Chair and the Vice Chair together do not constitute a quorum, and the Superintendent is not a member of the Committee in any event, nothing in the Open Meeting Law prohibits the Chair and Vice Chair from meeting with the Superintendent outside of noticed public meetings

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Chair, Vice Chair and superintendent effectively decided agenda placement among themselves, which should have been a full Committee decision.
allegations.key_passage: this allegation goes to the authority of individuals such as the Superintendent versus the Board to take action on particular matters, which is not a matter governed by the Open Meeting Law
